BuildContext.description:
Build engine context declared in ``[build_context]`` of ``.zenzic.toml``.

Tells Zenzic which documentation engine produced the site and which locale
directories are non-default translations.  Used by adapters to resolve
asset and page paths correctly.

engine.description: The build engine used by the documentation. Can be 'mkdocs', 'zensical', 'standalone', or 'auto'.
engine.title: Engine

default_locale.description: ISO 639-1 code of the default locale.
default_locale.title: Default Locale

base_url.description: The root URL where the documentation is hosted (e.g. `https://docs.zenzic.dev/`).
base_url.title: Base Url

fallback_to_default.description: When True, missing locale-tree assets/pages fall back to the default-locale tree. Set to False to report every missing locale file as an error.
fallback_to_default.title: Fallback To Default

offline_mode.description: When True, adapters force flat URL structure (e.g. use_directory_urls=False) for offline builds.
offline_mode.title: Offline Mode

BuildContext.title: BuildContext

CustomRuleConfig.description:
A single entry in the ``[[custom_rules]]`` TOML array.

Supports both regex-based line rules and Python class-based Custom Rule SDK v3 rules.

TOML example (regex)::

    [[custom_rules]]
    id = "ZZ-NOINTERNAL"
    pattern = "internal\.corp\.example\.com"
    message = "Internal hostname must not appear in public docs."
    severity = "error"

TOML example (SDK v3 Python class)::

    [[custom_rules]]
    class_name = "zenzic.sdk.examples.NoTodoRule"

id.description: Stable unique identifier for this rule (e.g. 'ZZ-MY-RULE').
id.title: Id

pattern.description: Regular-expression string applied to each content line.
pattern.title: Pattern

message.description: Human-readable explanation shown in the finding.
message.title: Message

class_name.description: Fully qualified Python class name for a Custom Rule SDK v3 rule.
class_name.title: Class Name

CustomRuleConfig.title: CustomRuleConfig

GovernanceConfig.description:
Governance toggles declared in ``[governance]``.

This section controls opt-in governance checks introduced in v0.8.

brand_obsolescence.description: Deprecated brand terms that activate Z601 BRAND_OBSOLESCENCE when present in docs source.
brand_obsolescence.title: Brand Obsolescence

per_file_ignores.description: Per-file suppression map (glob pattern -> finding codes). Example: {'blog/*.md': ['Z601']}. Security findings remain non-suppressible regardless of this map.
per_file_ignores.title: Per File Ignores

directory_policies.description: Strategic directory-level policy exemptions (glob pattern -> finding codes). Matched findings are removed before display with ZERO suppression debt cost. In --audit mode, exempted findings appear with a [POLICY_EXEMPTION] label. Intended for historical archives, SSOT registries, and blog directories. Security findings (Z201-Z204) bypass this exemption unconditionally.
directory_policies.title: Directory Policies

suppression_cap.description: Maximum number of active suppressions allowed before hard-failing the check pipeline.
suppression_cap.title: Suppression Cap

suppression_cap_scope.description: Suppression CAP scope. 'all' counts inline suppressions plus per-file configuration suppressions.
suppression_cap_scope.title: Suppression Cap Scope

suppression_cap_fail_hard.description: When True, exceeding suppression_cap causes immediate exit 1.
suppression_cap_fail_hard.title: Suppression Cap Fail Hard

GovernanceConfig.title: GovernanceConfig

cache_ttl_hours.description: Time-to-live for cached external links in hours.
cache_ttl_hours.title: Cache Ttl Hours

PoliciesConfig.description:
Declarative governance policies declared in ``[policies]`` (v0.28.0).

This section introduces the **Policy-as-Code Engine**, allowing project
maintainers to define deterministic, declarative rules that every
Markdown file must satisfy.  Policies are **opt-in**: an empty
``[policies]`` table (or no ``[policies]`` key at all) applies no
additional constraints and is fully backward-compatible.

TOML example::

    [policies]
    required_frontmatter_keys = ["title", "description", "author"]
    forbidden_external_domains = ["competitor.example.com", "legacy.corp"]

required_frontmatter_keys.description: List of frontmatter keys that MUST be present in every Markdown file. Missing keys emit Z610 REQUIRED_FRONTMATTER_MISSING. Policy is inactive when the list is empty (opt-in). Example: ["title", "description", "author"]
required_frontmatter_keys.title: Required Frontmatter Keys

forbidden_external_domains.description: List of external domain prefixes forbidden from appearing in any link (both native Markdown and raw HTML <a href>). Violations emit Z611 FORBIDDEN_DOMAIN_REFERENCE. Policy is inactive when the list is empty (opt-in). Example: ["competitor.example.com", "legacy.corp"]
forbidden_external_domains.title: Forbidden External Domains

forbidden_frontmatter_keys.description: List of frontmatter keys that MUST NOT exist in any Markdown file. Presence of any forbidden key emits Z612 FORBIDDEN_FRONTMATTER_KEY. Policy is inactive when the list is empty (opt-in). Example: ["draft", "internal_notes"]
forbidden_frontmatter_keys.title: Forbidden Frontmatter Keys

frontmatter_schema_match.description: Dictionary mapping frontmatter key names to RE2 regex patterns that the key's value must match. Mismatch emits Z613 FRONTMATTER_SCHEMA_MISMATCH. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: {"version": r"^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$"}
frontmatter_schema_match.title: Frontmatter Schema Match

allowed_external_domains.description: Zero-Trust whitelist of allowed external domain prefixes. When non-empty, ANY external link not matching this whitelist emits Z614 UNAPPROVED_DOMAIN_REFERENCE. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: ["zenzic.dev", "github.com"]
allowed_external_domains.title: Allowed External Domains

required_url_schemes.description: List of allowed URL scheme prefixes. Any link using a scheme not listed in this whitelist emits Z615 FORBIDDEN_URL_SCHEME. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: ["https", "mailto"]
required_url_schemes.title: Required Url Schemes

cross_namespace_restrictions.description: Dictionary mapping a source namespace path prefix to a list of forbidden target namespace path prefixes. Links crossing restricted boundaries emit Z616 CROSS_NAMESPACE_LINK_FORBIDDEN. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: {"docs/public": ["docs/internal"]}
cross_namespace_restrictions.title: Cross Namespace Restrictions

forbidden_content_patterns.description: List of RE2 regex patterns forbidden from appearing in prose content. Matches emit Z617 FORBIDDEN_CONTENT_PATTERN. Policy is inactive when the list is empty (opt-in). Example: ["\\bTODO\\b", "\\bFIXME\\b", "\\bconfidential\\b"]
forbidden_content_patterns.title: Forbidden Content Patterns

required_heading_patterns.description: List of RE2 regex patterns where each pattern MUST match at least one heading in the document. Missing matching headings emit Z618 REQUIRED_HEADING_PATTERN. Policy is inactive when the list is empty (opt-in). Example: ["^Overview$", "^License$"]
required_heading_patterns.title: Required Heading Patterns

max_document_complexity.description: Maximum allowed document complexity score (based on word count, heading depth, and link density). Documents exceeding this threshold emit Z619 MAX_DOCUMENT_COMPLEXITY. 0 disables complexity checking (opt-in).
max_document_complexity.title: Max Document Complexity

weasel_words.description: List of weasel words to detect in prose (e.g., 'clearly', 'simply', 'obviously'). Detected words emit Z519 WEASEL_WORDS. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: ["clearly", "simply", "obviously", "basically", "very"]
weasel_words.title: Weasel Words

enable_passive_voice_check.description: When True, enables heuristic passive voice detection (Z518 PASSIVE_VOICE_DETECTED). Strictly opt-in.
enable_passive_voice_check.title: Enable Passive Voice Check

required_table_columns.description: Dictionary mapping a heading/context pattern (or '*' for all tables) to a list of required column header names. Missing columns emit Z521 REQUIRED_TABLE_COLUMN. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: {"*": ["Status", "Description"], "^API Reference$": ["Method", "Endpoint"]}
required_table_columns.title: Required Table Columns

table_cell_enums.description: Dictionary mapping column header names to allowed string enum values. Cells with values outside this whitelist emit Z522 TABLE_CELL_ENUM. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: {"Status": ["draft", "review", "stable"]}
table_cell_enums.title: Table Cell Enums

required_heading_order.description: List of RE2 regex heading patterns that must appear in strictly ascending sequential order. Out-of-order headings emit Z523 HEADING_ORDER_VIOLATION. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: ["^Overview$", "^Usage$", "^API Reference$"]
required_heading_order.title: Required Heading Order

traceability_targets.description: Dictionary mapping a target documentation glob pattern to a list of source documentation glob patterns. Target documents not linked by at least one matching source document emit Z412 TRACEABILITY_BROKEN. Policy is inactive when empty (opt-in). Example: {"docs/specs/**": ["docs/architecture/**"]}
traceability_targets.title: Traceability Targets

PoliciesConfig.title: PoliciesConfig

ProjectMetadata.description:
Optional brand-integrity metadata declared in ``[project_metadata]``.

When ``obsolete_names`` is non-empty, Zenzic activates the Z905
BRAND_OBSOLESCENCE rule, which warns on every occurrence of a deprecated
brand term found in documentation source files.  Lines carrying a
``zenzic:ignore`` comment are silently skipped so intentional historical
references (e.g. in CHANGELOG files or ADR entries) are not flagged.
Use ``<!-- zenzic:ignore: Z905 -->`` in ``.md`` files and
``{/* zenzic:ignore: Z905 */}`` in ``.mdx`` files.

TOML example::

    [project_metadata]
    release_name = "MyRelease"
    obsolete_names = ["PreviousRelease"]
    # ADR files contain intentional historical references
    obsolete_names_exclude_patterns = [
        "CHANGELOG*.md",
        "community/developers/explanation/adr-*.mdx",
    ]

release_name.description: Current canonical brand/release name shown in Z905 remediation hints.
release_name.title: Release Name

obsolete_names_exclude_patterns.description: Glob patterns (relative to docs_dir) for files excluded from Z905. CHANGELOG*.md is excluded by default to allow historical prose.
obsolete_names_exclude_patterns.title: Obsolete Names Exclude Patterns

badge_stamp_files.description: Files updated by 'zenzic score --stamp'. Each file must contain a '<!-- zenzic:audit-badge -->' and/or '<!-- zenzic:score-badge -->' marker; the next non-empty line after each marker is replaced with deterministic audit and/or score badge URLs.
badge_stamp_files.title: Badge Stamp Files

ProjectMetadata.title: ProjectMetadata

docs_dir.description: Path to docs directory relative to repo root.
docs_dir.title: Docs Dir

excluded_dirs.description: Directories inside docs/ to exclude from orphan and snippet checks. User-provided entries are merged with the system guardrails (SYSTEM_EXCLUDED_DIRS) — they can never be removed.
excluded_dirs.title: Excluded Dirs

snippet_min_lines.description: Minimum lines for a code block to be checked (skip trivial one-liners).
snippet_min_lines.title: Snippet Min Lines

max_sentence_length.description: Maximum words allowed in a sentence before triggering Z511 EXCESSIVE_SENTENCE_LENGTH.
max_sentence_length.title: Max Sentence Length

placeholder_max_words.description: Pages with fewer than this many words are flagged as placeholders.
placeholder_max_words.title: Placeholder Max Words

placeholder_patterns.description: RE2-compatible regex patterns matched case-insensitively against each line. A match flags the page as Z501 PLACEHOLDER. Use \b word boundaries to avoid substring false positives (e.g. r'\bwip\b' matches 'WIP' but not 'wipe').
placeholder_patterns.title: Placeholder Patterns

excluded_assets.description: Asset paths (relative to docs_dir) excluded from the unused-assets check. Entries may be literal paths or glob patterns (fnmatch syntax: *, ?, []). Use this for files that are referenced by the build tool or theme templates rather than by Markdown pages. Ignores files that do not exist such as virtual indices.
excluded_assets.title: Excluded Assets

excluded_asset_dirs.description: Directories inside docs/ whose non-markdown files are excluded from the unused-assets check. Use this for theme override directories whose files are consumed by the build tool rather than referenced from Markdown pages.
excluded_asset_dirs.title: Excluded Asset Dirs

excluded_file_patterns.description: Filename glob patterns excluded from all checks (orphan detection, placeholder scanning, reference pipeline, and credential scanner). Use this for locale-suffixed files managed by i18n plugins (e.g. '*.it.md', '*.fr.md') or historical prose that contains intentional examples of secrets or deprecated syntax (e.g. 'CHANGELOG*.md').
excluded_file_patterns.title: Excluded File Patterns

excluded_build_artifacts.description: Glob patterns (relative to docs_dir) for assets generated at build time. Links to paths matching these patterns are not flagged as broken even when the file does not exist on disk at lint time — e.g. PDFs produced by the to-pdf plugin or ZIP archives assembled by CI. Example: ["pdf/*.pdf", "assets/bundle.zip"]
excluded_build_artifacts.title: Excluded Build Artifacts

respect_vcs_ignore.description: When True (default), Zenzic reads .gitignore files from the repository root and docs directory and excludes matching paths from all checks. This aligns with industry-grade static analysis standards (Ruff, Ripgrep, Black, Prettier) where VCS-ignored paths are transparently excluded. Set to False only to override this behaviour explicitly. Forced inclusions (included_dirs, included_file_patterns) override VCS exclusions, but System Guardrails are always enforced.
respect_vcs_ignore.title: Respect Vcs Ignore

included_dirs.description: Directory names inside docs/ that are forcefully included even when excluded by VCS ignore patterns or excluded_dirs. Forced inclusions cannot override System Guardrails (.git, .venv, etc.).
included_dirs.title: Included Dirs

included_file_patterns.description: Filename glob patterns (fnmatch syntax) forcefully included even when excluded by VCS ignore patterns or excluded_file_patterns. Use for build-generated documentation that should be linted despite being in .gitignore — e.g. 'api.generated.md'.
included_file_patterns.title: Included File Patterns

validate_same_page_anchors.description: When True, same-page anchor links (#section) are validated against the headings present in the source file. A link like [text](#missing) is reported as broken when no heading in the file produces that slug. Disabled by default because single-page anchor IDs can also be generated by HTML attributes, custom plugins, or build-time macros that are invisible at source-scan time.
validate_same_page_anchors.title: Validate Same Page Anchors

excluded_external_urls.description: External URLs (or URL prefixes) excluded from the broken-link check. A URL is skipped when it starts with any entry in this list. Use this for URLs that are valid but not yet publicly reachable at lint time (e.g. a GitHub repo not yet created, an internal service behind a firewall). Example: ["https://github.com/PythonWoods-Dev/zenzic"]
excluded_external_urls.title: Excluded External Urls

absolute_path_allowlist.description: List of absolute path prefixes allowed in links. Absolute path links matching any pattern in this list do not trigger Z105. If an entry in this list is never matched by any scanned absolute path link, it is reported as Z112 STALE_ALLOWLIST_ENTRY.
absolute_path_allowlist.title: Absolute Path Allowlist

origin_file.description: Path to the file this configuration was loaded from.
origin_file.title: Origin File

build_context.description: Build engine context for locale-aware path resolution.

fail_under.description: Minimum quality score (0–100). If the score falls below this value, zenzic score exits with code 1. 0 means no threshold (observational mode). The --fail-under CLI flag overrides this value when explicitly provided.
fail_under.title: Fail Under

strict.description: When True, treat warnings as errors and validate external URLs via network requests. Equivalent to passing --strict on every check all / score / diff invocation. The --strict CLI flag overrides this value for a single run.
strict.title: Strict

exit_zero.description: When True, zenzic check all always exits with code 0 even when issues are found. Issues are still printed and scored. Useful for observation-only pipelines where you want visibility without blocking. The --exit-zero CLI flag overrides this value for a single run.
exit_zero.title: Exit Zero

custom_rules.description: Project-specific lint rules declared inline in .zenzic.toml.  Each entry applies a regex pattern line-by-line to every .md file.  Example:  [[custom_rules]]  id='ZZ001'  pattern='TODO'  message='Remove before publish.'  severity='warning'
custom_rules.title: Custom Rules

project_metadata.description: Optional metadata used by remediation messaging and legacy compatibility.

governance.description: Governance toggles for ADR-012 checks. Prefer this section over legacy [project_metadata].obsolete_names.

policies.description: Declarative Policy-as-Code governance rules (v0.28.0). Opt-in: no constraints applied when section is absent or empty. See PoliciesConfig for available policy keys.

network.description: Network I/O settings for external link validation.

plugins.description: Explicit allow-list of external rule plugins to activate from the 'zenzic.rules' entry-point group. Core rules shipped by Zenzic are always enabled.
plugins.title: Plugins

forbidden_patterns.description: Z204 FORBIDDEN_TERM: literal strings (case-insensitive) whose presence in any documentation file triggers an exit-2 security breach. Populated by merging patterns from ``.zenzic.local.toml`` at runtime. Never declare these in the shared ``.zenzic.toml`` — use the git-ignored ``.zenzic.local.toml`` so private terms are never committed.
forbidden_patterns.title: Forbidden Patterns
